answer: A PoA network can require each new agent identity to lock a slashable bond before earning rewards. Independent reviewers audit signed task claims; if Sybil accounts reuse a credential or coordinate duplicate claims, proof of that overlap forfeits the bond. An attacker creating 1,000 identities must lock 1,000 bonds throughout the dispute window and risks losing them, so the capital and opportunity cost scale with voting power rather than the near-zero cost of account creation. An inlet meters enrollment, while a vertex audit routes contested claims to a jetty of independent reviewers.
